W5 (contrarian), after E022.
1. Noise. Rebuilding the same commit reshuffles accuracy by about 0.05 pp (E017 vs E019). Graph or kernel changes act like a fresh 3-seed draw, with a 3-seed SD of about 0.25 pp. My estimate of the tip's true mean is about 0.7555, so the real margin is about 0.25 pp. E016's 0.7607 was a high draw. E022 (SGD-group wd ×0.25) gave 0.7545: wd is a flat direction. Muon renormalizes the filters, so filter wd is inert. Hyperparameter nudges (LS 0.2, Muon lr ×1.5, wd) all land between 0.7537 and 0.7557. That is a plateau. Don't expect any time-neutral booster to give +0.3 pp.
2. Epoch dial. E020: −1 true epoch gave −10.5% time and about −0.3 pp against the true mean, so about 2.3 s/pp. The −0.5 point (I036) should land near 0.754 true and fail ~45% of 3-seed draws.
3. Architecture trades cost about the same as the dial or more. E021 got −7.8% time for −0.3 pp. Only half the MAC saving showed up as time, because of fixed costs, memory-bound BN/GELU, and Muon NS, which scales with params, not pixels. By a rough count, conv throughput is already high (about 2.7 GFLOP/sample → about 100+ TFLOP/s implied), so there is no big kernel lever left.
4. Final-map regime (my mechanism). The 2x2 valid stem plus 3 pools gives a 3×3 final map at 26–32 px and 2×2 at ≤24 px. E018 (28→24, i.e. 3×3→2×2) lost about 0.5 pp; E011 cut in both regimes and fell off a cliff. A competing explanation I can't rule out is FixRes-style apparent-object-size mismatch: the max-pool head sees different receptive-field coverage. Both predict that 26 px is cheap and 20 px early is near-free. They differ on 26 px: my mechanism predicts no cost; the scale explanation predicts a small cost.
5. Time model. Time ≈ Σ steps × (stem-output pixels), with about 70% of the theoretical saving realized, plus about 0.3–0.5 s fixed. The early 20 px phase saves about 2.5% and 26 px in the middle about 3%. Odd sizes (25×25) may tile worse.
6. Code facts: 3 Newton-Schulz steps; 238 true steps; the loss sits outside the compiled module, so per-phase LS costs no recompile; alpha is a Python float into foreach_lerp (no recapture).
Unsure: E019's held-out mean; judge-GPU transfer; whether 26 px keeps accuracy.
Best path: stack 20 px early + 26 px middle (about −5–6% time) with no epoch cut, then judge on 13 seeds. Only after that, spend leftover margin on −0.25 epoch.

forecasts.reason: 20 vs 24 px on 15% of steps is the same 2×2 regime, so the accuracy loss is small, but the time saving is only ~2.5%, short of the ≥4% the hypothesis requires
−0.5 epoch ≈ −5% time and −0.15 pp true; the 3-seed noise straddles 0.7545
26 px keeps the 3×3 final map, so the loss should be ≤0.1 pp for a ~3% time cut, unlike E018
A stronger mid-run pull slows the fast weights; the averaging plateau means no +0.3 pp
LS changes were flat in E013; the EfficientNetV2 effect needs large regularization ranges, not LS 0.15 vs 0.3 on a 9-epoch underfit run
Rough FLOP count implies ≥90 TFLOP/s for 32 px convs; the E021 shortfall comes from non-conv/fixed costs, not slow convs

cruxes: Does the 26 px middle phase (3×3 final map) keep accuracy within 0.1 pp on 13 seeds, which would separate the final-map-regime mechanism from a FixRes/object-scale explanation?
What is the tip's held-out 10-seed mean (E019 part 1)? It sets how much margin exists to spend on 20/26 px phases and an epoch trim.
What fraction of step time is non-conv (BN/GELU, Muon NS, Lookahead, augmentation)? It caps the payoff of all resolution and width cuts.
